team_news: Arsenal: Christos Tzolis is OUT for a few weeks (muscle/hamstring, picked up with Greece). Daily Cannon reports William Saliba OUT. Kai Havertz and (per reports) Ezri Konsa face late fitness tests. Declan Rice skipped England duty for load management and Arteta hopes he is available. Ben White and Cristhian Mosquera are back in full training. Max Dowman is fit. Piero Hincapie is listed as available in one report and a late call in another. Leeds: Daniel James is OUT (back injury from Wales duty), but he has only 52 minutes this season, all off the bench. Joe Rodon is still out (hamstring). Jean-Matteo Bahoya (ankle sprain, France U21) is a chance to play. Harry Wilson is back in training. Farke is expected to keep a largely unchanged XI.
form_notes: Arsenal are 2nd (W4 L1, GF8 GA4): W3-0 Coventry, W1-0 at Villa, W2-1 Chelsea, W2-0 at Sunderland, then L0-3 at Brighton in the last game before the break. Leeds are 5th and unbeaten (W2 D3, GF7 GA3): W1-0 at Forest, D1-1 Brentford, D1-1 at Brighton, W4-1 Newcastle, D0-0 Palace. Leeds have conceded only 3 goals, which is joint 2nd best in the league. Arsenal's games average 2.4 goals.
xg_notes: Arsenal xG for is about 8.5-9.0 over 5 games (sources vary; one has 6.8), and one source ranks them the best defence on xGA (4.59). Leeds xG for is about 7.2-7.7 (10th on Squawka's xG table). No reliable Leeds xGA found. H2H context only: Arsenal won both 2025-26 meetings, and Arteta is 4/4 in league games against Farke.
pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC): Arsenal 2-0, though one report says he floated 1-1 or 2-2 because of the international-break disruption. Squawka model: 1-0. PredictZ: 3-1. Betfanatics: 2-1. FiFPlay: 2-0. Jones Knows: not found.
reasoning: Opta (68.9%) and the market (about 69% after removing the margin) make Arsenal clear favourites, and their home defensive record plus elite xGA supports a home win. I shade that down to 61% for three reasons: Saliba is reported out, Arsenal were heavily beaten 0-3 at Brighton before the break, and Rice and Havertz were managed or doubtful over the international window. Leeds are unbeaten, have conceded 3 in 5 and have drawn 3 times, so a low-event game is more likely than a rout. With Arsenal at about 1.6-1.7 expected goals and Leeds at about 0.7, a Poisson model makes 1-0 the modal Arsenal-win score, just ahead of 2-0.
risks: If Arsenal score early, Leeds have to open up and the over/2-0+ scores come in. Leeds' set-piece threat and the post-break disruption could still produce a 1-1.

team_news: Sunderland: Brian Brobbey is OUT (hamstring, could return within a week). Daniel Ballard is OUT. Habib Diarra is absent but back in training. Wilson Isidor is expected to lead the line. Squawka reports Reinildo suspended, but this is unconfirmed elsewhere. Brighton: Yankuba Minteh, Mats Wieffer and Kaoru Mitoma are getting closer but not fit. Stefanos Tzimas and Evan Ferguson are still out. Both sides are expected in a 4-2-3-1 (Roefs and Verbruggen in goal).
form_notes: Sunderland are 14th (W1 D1 L3, GF6 GA10): L1-2 at Ipswich, W1-0 Fulham, D1-1 at Brentford, L0-2 Arsenal, L3-5 at Man City. Brighton are 3rd (W3 D1 L1, GF16 GA5): W4-0 Villa, L3-4 at Chelsea, D1-1 at Leeds, W5-0 at Coventry, W3-0 Arsenal. Brighton's away record is W1 D1 L1.
xg_notes: Brighton lead most xG tables with about 11.0-11.5 xG for (2.19/90). Sunderland's underlying numbers are much better than their results: Squawka has 9.21 xG for and 7.39 xGA (6th on its xG table), against actual figures of 6 scored and 10 conceded. H2H context only: Brighton won at the Stadium of Light last season (per Sutton).
pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC): 1-1. Squawka model: 0-1. Dimers model: 1-1 as the most likely score (12.1%). Statz: 1-1. Last Word on Football: 3-2. BetFanatics: 1-3. Livescore: Brighton to grind out a win.
reasoning: Opta (41.3%), the market (about 42% after removing the margin) and Dimers (39%) all make Brighton the narrow favourites, and their 16 goals and top xG back that up. I trim Brighton and lift the draw because Brighton's attack is depleted: Mitoma, Minteh, Tzimas and Ferguson are out, and Wieffer is out in midfield. Sunderland's xG (9.2 for, 7.4 against) suggests their poor results flatter Brighton's edge. The season's 32% draw rate also points to a tighter game than the 1X2 suggests. Brighton remain my single most likely result, so the primary pick is a one-goal away win (1-2), with BTTS supported by both sides' chance creation. 1-1 is nearly as likely and is my strongest draw candidate if the panel wants more draws.
risks: This is essentially a three-way coin flip. 1-1 is probably the single most likely scoreline, and a Sunderland home win at 30% is very live given their underlying numbers.

form_notes: Chelsea are 10th (W2 D1 L2, GF10 GA12) and winless in 3: W3-2 at Fulham, W4-3 Brighton, L1-2 at Arsenal, D2-2 Hull, L0-3 at Brentford. All five Chelsea games went over 2.5 and four had BTTS. Bournemouth are 17th (W0 D3 L2, GF6 GA8): L1-2 at Man City, D1-1 Everton, D2-2 at Newcastle, D2-2 Brentford, L0-1 at Liverpool. Bournemouth's only defeats were by one goal, at City and Liverpool.
xg_notes: Chelsea xG for is about 7.3-7.75, mid-table (12th on Planet Football's xG table). Bournemouth: xGA 5.71 (Squawka), about 7 per xGstat, and 5.3 (7th) per an older Planet Football table. xG for is about 8 per xGstat, so their underlying numbers are better than 17th place suggests. H2H context only: Chelsea are unbeaten in their last 9 top-flight meetings (W4 D5, per The Analyst).
pundits: Chris Sutton (BBC): Chelsea 3-1. Betfanatics: 2-1. Footballwhispers: 2-1. Dimers model: 2-1 as the most likely score (9.6%). Sports Interaction: 2-2. Bet365 tip: Chelsea and BTTS at 15/8. Jones Knows: not found.
reasoning: Opta has Chelsea at 51.8%, and the market at about 58% after removing the margin. I go below both because Chelsea are winless in 3 and conceding 2.4 per game, and Palmer, Joao Pedro, James and Caicedo are all doubtful. Bournemouth are winless but competitive: they have three draws, one-goal defeats at City and Anfield, and decent xGA, and their pricing looks too long. Chelsea at home are still the most likely winners. Every Chelsea game has been high-event, so a one-goal home win with both teams scoring (2-1) is the natural primary. The draw is strongly live, at 1-1 or 2-2.
risks: If Palmer and Joao Pedro both miss, Chelsea's attack is blunted and 1-1 becomes the likelier score. If both start, Chelsea could win more comfortably, as in Sutton's 3-1.
